strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor today on this abrasive surface. Managing the tires through the long runs will be crucial.
The pit window is expected to be around lap 20 to 25, depending on the tire wear. A well-timed pit stop could be the difference between winning and losing.
With such a short lap length, traffic management will be a challenge for the drivers, especially during the pit stop phase.
Fuel consumption is always a concern here. The drivers will need to manage their fuel carefully to make it to the end.
The undercut can be very powerful here at the Red Bull Ring. Teams will be looking to exploit that advantage.
The relatively short lap means the pit lane loss is quite low, making multiple stop strategies viable.
The high altitude affects the engine performance. Teams will be adjusting their engine maps to compensate for the thinner air.
A one-stop strategy is likely to be the preferred choice, but a safety car could throw a wrench into the works.

The sun is beating down on the Red Bull Ring. It's going to be a hot and challenging race for the drivers.
